name: Deloitte
summary: Deloitte's interviews usually mix behavioural questions with a case or technical problem for the business you've applied to (audit, tax, consulting or advisory), and many roles end with a conversation with a partner or director. For campus hiring, candidates commonly report an online assessment first and, in India, a group discussion for some roles. Deloitte publishes five Shared Values, including 'Serve with integrity' and 'Take care of each other'.

covers: Your studies or current role in two or three lines, starting with what's most relevant to this job
One or two achievements that show analytical, technical or client-facing skills
Why you're applying to this business at Deloitte, as a bridge to the rest of the interview

questions.text: A client's sales dropped 20% this quarter. How would you find out why?
covers: Clarifying questions first: which products, regions and channels, and whether the whole market fell
A clear structure: price versus volume, then customers, competitors and changes inside the company
The most likely cause, the data you'd use to test it, and a first recommendation

questions.text: Tell me about a time you persuaded someone who disagreed with you.
covers: What they believed and why it was reasonable from their side
How you made your case: evidence, a small trial, or finding common ground
The outcome, and what you learnt about persuading people
What draws you to client work, shown by something you've done (a project, an internship, a competition)
Something specific about Deloitte: a business, a service line or a kind of project you want to work on
How your skills fit the role you've applied for

questions.text: Tell me about a time a teammate wasn't doing their share. What did you do?
covers: What was slipping and how it affected the team's deadline
How you raised it with them privately and found out why
What changed, and how you kept the working relationship good

questions.text: Describe a time you noticed something that didn't look right and raised it, even though it was awkward.
covers: What you noticed and how you checked it before speaking up
Who you told, and how you put it without blaming anyone
What happened next and why raising it was the right call

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to learn a new tool or subject quickly to deliver on time.
covers: Why you needed it and how little time you had
How you learnt it: what you read, built or asked
What you delivered, and how well it held up

questions.text: A client wants to move its finance systems to the cloud. What would you ask in the first meeting?
covers: The business reason: cost, speed, ageing systems or growth
What exists today: systems, data, integrations, users and any regulatory limits
Risks and timing: data migration, security, downtime, training, and how success will be measured

questions.text: Walk me through how you'd estimate the number of cups of coffee sold in Bengaluru on a weekday.
covers: A clear starting point, such as population or number of cafés and offices
Splitting by who drinks coffee and how often, with round numbers you say out loud
A final figure, a quick sense check, and which assumption matters most

questions.text: Explain what an external auditor does and why investors rely on audited financial statements.
covers: An independent check that the statements give a true and fair view, under the accounting rules that apply
How auditors gather evidence: testing samples, confirming balances, understanding controls
Why independence and professional scepticism matter to investors and lenders

questions.text: Explain the difference between a relational database and a NoSQL database, and when you'd choose each for a client project.
covers: Relational: tables, fixed schema, joins and transactions; NoSQL: flexible documents or key-value data at scale
A client example for each, such as finance ledgers versus product catalogues or event logs
The trade-offs you'd explain to the client: consistency, scaling, skills and cost

questions.text: You're implementing a new system and the client's team keeps resisting it. How would you get them on board?
covers: Finding out why: fear of extra work, lost control, or real gaps in the system
Involving key users early, showing quick wins and training them in their own processes
Keeping the client's sponsor informed and agreeing what success looks like

questions.text: Which of Deloitte's businesses do you want to work in, for example audit, tax, consulting or advisory, and why?
covers: A clear choice, linked to your studies, skills or experience
What you know about the work people at your level do there
What you hope to learn in your first two years

questions.text: What questions do you have for us?
covers: One or two specific questions about the team's clients, projects or training
A question that shows you've listened during the interview
Nothing you could have found on the careers site in a minute

tips: Structure answers out loud: 'I'd look at three things…'.
For case questions, ask clarifying questions before you answer.
Know which business and service line you've applied to; audit, tax, technology consulting and risk interviews ask quite different technical questions.
Bring one project you can explain end to end: the problem, your part, the tools you used and what the client or user got.
In a partner round, expect broader questions on business news and why you want client work; read up on one or two industries you'd like to serve.
Prepare a short story for each Shared Value, especially integrity and teamwork; behavioural questions often map to them.

rounds: Online application, with an assessment for some roles
First-round interview: behavioral questions and a case or technical problem
Final round with a partner or director
